Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (US Department of State or state Secretary of State); consular legalization only if issuing state is not an Apostille Convention signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Secretary / board of directors of the foreign parent corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille applied to the notarized secretary certificate; consular legalization fallback for non-Apostille states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and FINTRAC administrative designations; PEP status assessed per PCMLTFA definitions for foreign and domestic PEPs. Standard, not simplified, customer due diligence applies; absence of direct customer financial custody for ad-supported hyper-casual games supports a 'Low' AML risk rating with annual re-review; discrepancies trigger a suspicious transaction report under PCMLTFA s. 7.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Registry via BC OneStop / Corporate Online (corponline.gov.bc.ca) — Business Registry of British Columbia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English or French. Non-official-language names are transliterated into the Roman alphabet where needed; the registrar may reject names that are not clearly distinguishable in English or French. Distinctive invented words, common in hyper-casual gaming, are acceptable. For ULCs, the suffix 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' is standard practice; BCBCA ss. 22(1)–22(3) restrict the use of limited-liability elements such as 'Limited', 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' in the name of an unlimited liability company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurance, Loan, Broker — require financial regulator approval
University, College, Institute, Architect, Engineer, Lawyer, Notary, Physician — require professional regulator consent
Royal, Crown, Government, Canada, British Columbia, Municipality, Police — imply Crown or government sponsorship
Red Cross, Red Crescent, United Nations — internationally protected emblems
Cooperative — authorized use limited to prescribed cooperative entities
Misleading legal elements such as SARL, GmbH or Inc. implying limited liability where inconsistent with ULC status
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing BC or extra-provincial registered company or registered trademark
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected under BCBCA ss. 22–23: (i) re-file a new Name Request with amended distinctive elements (CAD 30 fee); (ii) submit a written reconsideration request to the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of refusal, attaching mark-search evidence and a legal argument on distinctiveness; (iii) after exhaustion of administrative reconsideration, apply by petition to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c. 241. No extension is available for a name reservation after the 56-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible if the address is a physical BC street address at which legal process can be served and the corporate/records office is accessible during normal business hours (BCBCA ss. 50–51). P.O. boxes and mail-forwarding-only addresses are non-compliant. Service-provider registered offices, including a BC law firm's office, are accepted; for gaming ULCs with no physical BC presence, a law-firm office address satisfies the statutory mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated ≤10% cumulative probability over the first three years. FINTRAC and CRA focus inspections on higher-risk sectors, and a low-risk, ad-monetized game publisher without consumer funds custody is unlikely to receive unannounced spot checks beyond registry compliance verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 10-12, 105, 118 and provisions respecting unlimited liability companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Combined Notice of Articles and Certificate of Incorporation application (Form 1) submitted electronically through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A share block may be issued for any consideration authorized by the directors, and consideration must be paid before or at issue. No escrow account is mandated; the registered office must be located in British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole incorporator adopts the filed Articles and Notice of Articles, forming an unlimited liability corporation under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). RESOLVED, that one Common Share be issued to the initial subscriber for no consideration, and the first board of directors be constituted. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address set out in the Notice of Articles. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President, [name] Secretary, and [name] Chief Financial Officer, with authority to execute contracts, open bank accounts, and complete regulatory filings. RESOLVED, that the directors and officers take all necessary steps to obtain corporate identifiers and commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and corporate address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services - BC Corporate Online name request system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request or NUANS search to avoid conflict with existing BC corporate names. If a name is reserved, accept the reservation confirmation. Confirm the proposed registered office is a physical address in British Columbia and is not a post office box.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, either file under a new name using the same application pathway or adopt an incorporated number. A formal name objection may be cured by amending the proposed name and refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare ULC Articles containing the unlimited liability statement and any share class provisions. Complete Notice of Articles (Form 1) with company name, registered office address, and first director details. Execute the director's consent and any required registered office consent forms.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a consent or address, obtain an updated consent or corrected address and refile the affected page through BC Corporate Online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, download and retain the certificate and the stamped Notice of Articles. Verify the legal name, jurisdiction, date, and registered office particulars are accurate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clerical errors appear in the certificate or Notice of Articles, request a correction from the Registrar under applicable correction provisions and file a corrected Notice of Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational board resolution and share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors (sole or titular director)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or execute a written resolution in lieu of a meeting. Adopt the Articles and Notice of Articles, issue one common share to the initial subscriber pursuant to the first board resolution, appoint officers, record the registered office, and create the statutory minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any purported issuance exceeds authorized capital or lacks board authority, pass a curative board resolution and reissue the share certificate in conformity with the BCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation statutory filings and CRA registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online; BC Registries for annual reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online. Register for GST/HST and payroll accounts if the entity has taxable Canadian revenue or employees. Initiate the first BC annual report filing in accordance with the BCA's prescribed period. If a physical office is established, register for a municipal business licence as required by the local by-law.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA returns the application for inconsistent data, verify the corporate identity against the BC Corporate Registry, correct the CRA application, and resubmit via Business Registration Online.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no provincial industrial or manufacturing licensing applies to ISIC 5820 software publishing. If a physical studio is opened, the local municipal licence office, e.g. City of Vancouver Business Licence Office, administers a general business licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure digital game publishing; an optional general municipal business licence (e.g. Vancouver Business Licence) applies to physical office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not triggered - no designated project under the British Columbia Environmental Assessment Act; office-based software publishing is exempt from EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, process VOCs, or point-source air emissions. E-waste from IT equipment must be handled under the BC Recycling Regulation; discharges, if any, must comply with municipal sewer and solid waste bylaws and federal/provincial water quality standards, exceedance-free.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Premises must satisfy the BC Building Code and Fire Code occupancy requirements and, where applicable, obtain a fire safety certificate. WorksafeBC occupational health and safety compliance, including employer registration and workplace inspections, is required. No civil-defence clearance applies to a non-industrial, office-based software publisher.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal GST/HST, T2 corporate income tax and Business Number issuance; online portal is CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO). The British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Provincial Tax Services, administers the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BC ULC must first be incorporated under the BC Business Corporations Act via BC Corporate Online, obtaining a BC incorporation number. Next, register with CRA through BRO to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and activate program accounts RC0001 (GST/HST), RC0002 (T2 corporate income tax) and RP0001 (payroll). As a corporation incorporated in Canada, the ULC is a Canadian resident corporation and must file T2 returns. GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies other than zero-rated supplies exceed C$30,000; voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits when supplies are exclusively zero-rated exports. For PST, submit BC Taxpayer Registration (FIN 419) to the BC Ministry of Finance before making taxable sales of software or digital products consumable in BC; no de minimis threshold applies for PST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation under ITA Part I for domestic purposes, but under Article IV(7) of the Canada-US Tax Treaty its shareholders may file a US federal check-the-box election on Form 8832 to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity (single US shareholder) or partnership (multiple US shareholders), making it fiscally transparent solely for US federal tax purposes. Canada requires no parallel domestic election, so the entity remains an entity-level taxpayer in Canada; hybrid-mismatch outcomes are mitigated under the OECD BEPS Action 2 framework reflected in Canadian treaty policy statements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax; 5% in British Columbia, no provincial HST) plus BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST at 7%); non-resident digital services may use the CRA Simplified GST/HST Registration Framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 under ETA s. 148; registration is required once worldwide taxable supplies other than financial services and sales of capital real property exceed C$30,000 in the current calendar quarter or over the preceding four calendar quarters. Under the simplified framework, a non-resident vendor without a Canadian establishment must register once its taxable supplies to Canadian recipients exceed C$30,000 in a 12-month period. Zero-rated export supplies to AdMob and AppLovin typically fall outside the counting of taxable supplies for threshold purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based continuous transaction control regime. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) by registrants with total annual taxable supplies above C$1.5M, and T2 returns must be e-filed for corporations with gross revenue exceeding C$1M. The voluntary pan-Canadian B2B e-invoicing framework is built on the Peppol UBL/BIS 3.0 standard and operates through certified service providers without government clearance middleware.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI, Part V. Services supplied to a non-resident — including advertising inventory services sold to non-resident ad networks (AdMob, AppLovin) and licensing/distribution services to non-resident app-store operators — are zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI, Part V, s. 7 provided the recipient is a non-resident at the time payment becomes due, the service is not connected to real or tangible property located in Canada, and the service is not performed wholly in Canada in circumstances where the recipient is deemed to be in Canada. The ULC must obtain and retain evidence of each payer's non-resident status and the foreign consumption of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Coding Form B13A (Export Declaration) or CERS/NPDS electronic export report for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing export from Canada
Commercial invoice and ad-network/app-store agreements identifying the non-resident counterparty and foreign payee
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statements showing foreign-currency consideration credited to the Canadian bank account
Tax residency certificates for the non-resident recipients; all books and records retained for at least six years under ETA s. 286 and ITA s. 230
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the original assessment, or indefinitely where misrepresentation, negligence, or wilful default is established; deficient export evidence causes zero-rating to be denied and full 5% GST plus retroactive interest to be charged. False statements or omissions attract the ETA s. 285(1) penalty (greater of C$250 and 5% of the amount assessed), and gross negligence on the income tax side triggers ITA s. 163(2) at 50% of the understated tax; deliberate export-fraud schemes are subject to criminal prosecution. BC PST clawbacks and penalties are enforced separately by the BC Ministry of Finance under the Provincial Sales Tax Act and the provincial Tax Administration Act.

stage_4.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank of Canada)
stage_4.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency CAD/USD Business Banking; optional Capital Escrow sub-account for platform reserves)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: British Columbia Annual Report for Unlimited Liability Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Registry, Government of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Two months after each incorporation anniversary date; e.g., an anniversary of July 1 requires filing by September 1.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to CAD $300 (approx. USD $220) may apply; failure to file for two consecutive annual reporting cycles permits the Registrar to strike the ULC off the register under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act, causing loss of corporate capacity until restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Provincial Combined)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the return is due by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay for up to 12 months; daily interest accrues on unpaid amounts; gross negligence and false-statement penalties may apply under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return for Annual Filing Filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the corporation's fiscal year-end if the ULC qualifies for annual filing; for a December 31 year-end, the return is due by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of net tax owing plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; interest at prescribed CRA rates is charged on overdue remittances; continued non-compliance may lead to revocation of GST/HST registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed by the British Columbia Business Corporations Act solely based on revenue, assets, or shareholding for a non-reporting ULC. An audit becomes mandatory only if the corporation is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, if shareholders validly pass a special resolution requiring an audit, or if a court orders one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A non-reporting BC ULC may prepare financial statements under IFRS or ASPE as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook; for income tax purposes, the CRA accepts financial statements prepared under either framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. Ownership is maintained continuously through entries in the Register of Members and Register of Transfers. Any transfer of ULC shares must be recorded without undue delay; the annual report confirms the current directors and registered office but does not require a UBO schedule.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD $350 - $1,200 per year (approximately CAD $475 - $1,600) depending on the registered office/agent service provider in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD $5,000 - $25,000 per engagement when an audit is required, based on transaction volume and complexity; for a non-reporting ULC without a shareholder-required audit, no statutory audit fee is incurred.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal Part I rate after the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general reduction, plus 12% British Columbia provincial corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: combined 11% (9% federal + 2% BC) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit: 35% refundable for CCPCs or 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs; BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit: 17.5% refundable on eligible BC labour expenditures for qualifying game development; Canadian Digital Services Tax (3%) applies only to groups with global revenue of at least CAD 20 billion and Canadian digital services revenue of at least CAD 20 million, and is therefore not applicable to the hyper-casual SME profile.
